chain.label: No fail-safe for total acme nut thread loss
chain.trigger: no contingency for the complete loss of the acme nut threads was incorporated into the design for the longitudinal trim control system

chain.label: Alaska Airlines extended jackscrew lubrication interval, FAA accepted
chain.trigger: In July 1996, the jackscrew assembly lubrication task was removed from the A check and placed on a time-controlled task card with a maximum interval of 8 months... about 2,550 flight hours

chain.label: Alaska Airlines extended end play check interval, FAA approved
chain.trigger: At the time of the flight 261 accident, Alaska Airlines' end play check interval was every 30 months, or about every 9,550 flight hours

chain.label: Scheduled jackscrew lubrications missed or inadequately performed
chain.trigger: there was no effective lubrication on the acme screw and nut interface at the time of the Alaska Airlines flight 261 accident

chain.label: Excessive wear of acme nut threads (~90% of thickness gone)
chain.trigger: The thread failure was caused by excessive wear resulting from Alaska Airlines' insufficient lubrication of the jackscrew assembly

caused_by.evidence: the excessive and accelerated wear of the accident jackscrew assembly acme nut threads was the result of insufficient lubrication
extended lubrication interval... increased the likelihood that a missed or inadequate lubrication would result in excessive wear of the acme nut threads
extended end play check interval and the FAA's approval of that extension, which allowed the excessive wear of the acme nut threads to progress to failure without the opportunity for detection

chain.label: Acme nut threads sheared off by acme screw
chain.trigger: the worn threads inside the horizontal stabilizer acme nut were incrementally sheared off by the acme screw and were completely sheared off during the accident flight

caused_by.evidence: approximately 90 percent of the thread thickness had worn away before the remainder of the threads sheared off

chain.label: Horizontal stabilizer jammed, unresponsive to trim commands
chain.trigger: as the airplane passed through 23,400 feet, the acme screw and nut jammed, preventing further movement of the horizontal stabilizer until the initial dive

caused_by.evidence: loads resulting from the acme screw threads pulling upward across the remaining ridges after the shearing

chain.label: Crew troubleshooting beyond checklist; primary trim motor re-activated
chain.trigger: the earlier repeated attempts to activate the primary trim system went well beyond what was called for in Alaska Airlines' checklist procedures

caused_by.evidence: we did both the pickle switch and the suitcase handles and it ran away full nose trim down

chain.label: Jam released; initial dive from 31,050 ft
chain.trigger: the accident airplane's initial dive from 31,050 feet began when the jam between the acme screw and nut was overcome as a result of the operation of the primary trim motor

caused_by.evidence: the torque created by the primary trim motor when the captain activated the primary trim system at 1609:16 apparently provided enough force to overcome the jam
Release of the jam allowed the acme screw to pull up through the acme nut, causing the horizontal stabilizer leading edge to move upward

chain.label: Low-cycle fatigue fracture of the acme screw torque tube
chain.trigger: the cause of the final dive was the low-cycle fatigue fracture of the torque tube

caused_by.evidence: the magnitude and frequency of the loads on the torque tube after complete shearing of the acme nut threads, in combination with an offset loading condition, would be sufficient to initiate and propagate low-cycle fatigue cracking
Calculated tension loads on the acme screw between the first and second dives were considerably larger than the loads encountered in the normal operational envelope

chain.label: Uncontrollable nose-down pitchover, airplane inverted
chain.trigger: The resulting upward movement of the horizontal stabilizer leading edge created an excessive upward aerodynamic tail load, which caused an uncontrollable downward pitching of the airplane from which recovery was not possible

caused_by.evidence: followed by the failure of the vertical stabilizer tip fairing brackets, which allowed the horizontal stabilizer leading edge to move upward significantly beyond what is permitted by a normally operating jackscrew assembly
Also contributing to the accident was the absence on the McDonnell Douglas MD-80 of a fail-safe mechanism to prevent the catastrophic effects of total acme nut thread loss

chain.label: Impact with Pacific Ocean near Anacapa Island
chain.trigger: flight 261, a McDonnell Douglas MD-83, N963AS, crashed into the Pacific Ocean about 2.7 miles north of Anacapa Island, California

caused_by.evidence: the airplane remained near inverted, and its pitch oscillated in the nose-down position until it impacted the ocean

chain.label: All 88 occupants killed; airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The 2 pilots, 3 cabin crewmembers, and 83 passengers on board were killed, and the airplane was destroyed by impact forces

caused_by.evidence: all of the accident airplane's occupants died as a result of blunt force impact trauma
